summary: NASA has initiated a major push for lunar infrastructure, opening a $10 billion lander pool, ordering a nuclear-powered rover, and issuing new awards for surface transportation, technology, and science projects alongside a $1 million student moon base challenge. To support the expanding Artemis program, the agency is also opening applications to recruit its next class of astronauts. In military developments, U.S. Air Force leadership announced plans to equip C-17 cargo aircraft with palletized cruise missiles. On the scientific front, data from the James Webb Space Telescope revealed more than 100 magnified stellar events in the Dragon galaxy, while cosmological researchers ruled out "stupendously large" primordial black holes as a dark matter source. Looking ahead, international spaceflight observers should watch China's upcoming Shenzhou 24 mission, which is set to carry a Pakistani astronaut who will become the first foreign national on China's space station.
